title: Long lines and accuracy under fatigue

D0.outcome: Explains why accuracy falls in a long game and what routine slows the fall.

D1.outcome: Calculates a ten-ply line at the end of a long training session with no more errors than in the fresh baseline.

D2.outcome: In a two-hour set of positions, keeps the rate of blunders flat across the second half, as the log shows.

D3.outcome: Names a personal fatigue marker and the routine that corrects it, and the log confirms it works over several sessions.

misconceptions: Fatigue only affects speed, not accuracy.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S4 (Kotov, Aagaard, Ramesh, Dvoretsky, Rowson, Heisman, all [R] in the map) (CAL.ENDURANCE T6-7)
conditions: Session length is long enough to show a fall in accuracy.
contrasts: The first-hour accuracy figure is used as the standard for the third hour.
Practising long lines only when fresh, then meeting them tired in tournaments.
note: Few sources in the sheets; mainly from the map's S4 and S10 descriptions.
